plan: With a private value of $31, I want to maximize my potential profit. Since values are randomly drawn between $0-$49, other bidders likely have values around $24.5 on average. A dominant strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to reduce overpaying. I'll aim to bid around my value minus a small buffer, anticipating rational behavior from other bidders who will also try to minimize overpayment. I'll bid $28 to create a strategic margin.

With a private value of $37, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are drawn randomly between $0-$49, rational bidders will likely bid strategically near their value. A pure dominant strategy is impossible. I'll aim to bid slightly above my value but not excessively high, anticipating other bidders might bid around their own values. A bid around $40-$42 seems reasonable to balance winning probability and potential profit margin.

My value is $11. In a first-price sealed bid auction with rational opponents, I want to bid strategically. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, opponents might bid near their own values. A pure dominant strategy doesn't exist. I'll aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit, accounting for potential opponent behavior. A bid around $9-$10 seems reasonable - low enough to potentially win if opponents have lower values, but not so low that I miss winning.
